Studies in men being treated for prostate cancer also found anastrozole to be ineffective for the prevention12,13 and treatment12 of gynaecomastia associated with bicalutamide ther- apy; in comparison, tamoxifen was effective in both studies. Where drug therapy is unsuccessful, or the breast enlargement is long-standing, surgical removal of breast tissue is advocated.2,3 Prophylactic low-dose radiotherapy to the breast can significant- ly reduce the risk of gynaecomastia and breast pain in men un- dergoing anti-androgen treatment for prostate cancer,2 although comparative studies suggest that it may be less effective than tamoxifen.14,15 1.
